problem: Are there infinitely many Lehmer pairs ?
missing_details: Definition of a Lehmer pair via an explicit inequality
Definition and ordering of the zeros γ_n of the Riemann zeta function
Specification that zeros are nontrivial zeros on the critical line 1/2 + iγ
The constant C and its required bound C>5/4 in the definition
Clarification that γ_n and γ_{n+1} refer to consecutive zeros
refined_question: Let {γ_n} be the imaginary parts of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function ζ(s) on the critical line, ordered so that γ_n ≤ γ_{n+1}. A pair (γ_n,γ_{n+1}) is called a Lehmer pair if there exists a fixed constant C>5/4 such that 1/(γ_{n+1}−γ_n)² ≥ C ∑_{m≠n,n+1} [1/(γ_m−γ_n)² + 1/(γ_m−γ_{n+1})²]. Is the set of all Lehmer pairs infinite?
justification: The original problem name asks for infinitely many Lehmer pairs but does not specify what a Lehmer pair is, nor the notation and context necessary for a standalone understanding. The refined question includes the definition of γ_n as imaginary parts of consecutive nontrivial zeros on the critical line, the precise inequality characterizing Lehmer pairs with the constant bound C>5/4, and then asks whether infinitely many such pairs exist, faithfully reflecting the canonical formulation from Wikipedia.
